description:
Passionate software developer and data analytics enthusiast focused on building clean, high-performance web applications and spatial tools.

Executing a solo project for the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge—building a single-page dashboard that evaluates lunar landing sites using 3D mapping and terrain analytics.

Tech Stack: • Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Three.js • Backend: Java Spring Boot (REST APIs)

Executing independently, but open to connecting and sharing ideas!
summary:
I built the Lunar Landing Site Navigator, an interactive 3D web simulator designed to evaluate candidate landing sites near the Moon’s South Pole.

Landing in this region is challenging because steep crater walls and long shadows can abruptly cut off solar power and Direct-to-Earth communications. Using Three.js for 3D visualization and a Java Spring Boot backend paired with a spherical ephemeris calculation engine, my application turns complex orbital math into an intuitive planning workspace.

Users can evaluate preset Artemis-region targets, such as Shackleton Crater Rim and Malapert Mountain or switch to Custom Mode to test any lunar coordinates, elevation, and local terrain horizon mask. By adjusting the date and scrubbing through a 24-hour UTC timeline, users can observe live lighting shifts on a 3D lunar globe, monitor real-time Sun and Earth elevation angles, check overall site suitability scores, and export the full telemetry dataset to CSV in one click.

This project gives mission planners, researchers, and students a fast, visual way to identify safe, power-rich, and communication-friendly landing windows without digging through raw orbital tables.
details:
The Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an interactive 3D simulation and mission-planning dashboard designed to evaluate solar illumination and Earth communication windows near the Moon’s South Pole. Users can select curated Artemis-region presets, such as Shackleton Crater Rim and Malapert Mountain or switch to Custom Mode to test any lunar coordinates, surface elevation, and local terrain horizon mask. Using a real-time spherical ephemeris calculation engine, the application computes Sun and Earth elevation and azimuth angles across any selected date and 24-hour UTC timeline, updating a 3D lunar globe and calculating an overall site suitability score.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Planning landings near the Lunar South Pole is difficult because low sun angles and steep crater walls create long, shifting shadows that can cut off solar power and Direct-to-Earth communications. Instead of requiring planners, researchers, or students to dig through raw orbital tables and static spreadsheets, this tool translates complex lunar geometry into immediate visual telemetry. Users can scrub through a 24-hour forecast, spot optimal power and communication windows at a glance, and export the full telemetry dataset to CSV in one click for offline mission analysis.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Frontend & 3D Visualization: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript, and Three.js (for rendering the interactive 3D lunar globe, lighting angles, and target pins).
  • Backend & Architecture: Java and Spring Boot (REST API architecture for site presets and telemetry processing), paired with a client-side ephemeris math fallback engine for zero-latency browser execution.
  • Development & Deployment: Visual Studio Code, GitHub (https://github.com/tkeswani007/Lunar-Landing-Site-Navigator) and Netlify for live cloud hosting ( https://lunar-landing-site-navigator.netlify.app )

Creativity & Key Factors Considered

To make complex orbital mechanics feel intuitive, I designed a sleek mission-control interface that pairs an interactive 3D lunar globe with live 24-hour forecast charts allowing users to visually see shadows move across craters while tracking exact telemetry metrics. Key factors considered during development included local terrain horizon masks (accounting for nearby crater rims blocking low-angle sunlight or Earth line-of-sight), responsive client-side performance so the app runs smoothly in any browser without backend bottlenecks, and clean CSV data portability for engineering workflows.
